title: Watching Steve Reich watch Steve Reich
gist: Marking Steve Reich's 90th birthday, James Hardie recalls a 2016 outdoor performance of Electric Counterpoint and Different Trains at Liverpool's Edge Hill Station, arguing Reich is one of the rare living classical composers whose minimalist sound world has transcended genre, appealing to purists and acid ravers alike.

insights.claim: Steve Reich is one of the rare living classical composers to attain status as a major cultural figure with a sound world that transcends genre; only fellow minimalists Philip Glass and Arvo Pärt can claim similar malleability.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Crossover appeal is what sustains a contemporary classical composer's cultural and commercial relevance.
insights.quote: His style of composition appeals to classical purists and acid ravers alike.
insights.locator: Steve Reich is one of those rare

insights.claim: Electric Counterpoint (1987), first recorded by Pat Metheny, has been embraced beyond classical audiences: sampled in The Orb's 'Little Fluffy Clouds', remixed by Röyksopp, and performed live by Radiohead's Jonny Greenwood.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Sampling and remix culture extends the catalogue value of minimalist works into popular music.

insights.claim: Reich's overlapping rhythms and driving pulse seem to tap into something deeply woven into the modern psyche, explaining his enduring appeal.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Interpretive claim about why minimalism resonates broadly.
insights.quote: seems to tap into something deeply woven into the modern psyche
insights.locator: Steve Reich is one of those rare

insights.claim: Different Trains (1988) parallels Reich's childhood train trips across America between divorced parents with the journeys Jews made across Europe during the Holocaust, deriving melodic motifs from speech snippets including Holocaust survivors.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Shows how documentary sampling can carry historical memory in contemporary composition.

insights.claim: At the 2016 Edge Hill performance, a real train passed through the station as Different Trains' closing melodies thinned out, creating an extraordinarily resonant moment.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Site-specific staging can amplify a work's impact.
insights.quote: a real train trundled through the station
insights.locator: The closing moments of that concert

insights.claim: The 80th-birthday concert, presented by arts organisation Metal, took place outdoors at Liverpool's Edge Hill Station, opened in 1836 and described as the oldest active passenger railway station in the world.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Heritage infrastructure repurposed for arts programming.

insights.claim: The author encountered Reich, grouchy but at ease in old age, watching a documentary about himself, and saw him jump onto the sound desk mid-show because he was unhappy with the mix — reportedly a regular occurrence.
insights.speaker: James Hardie
insights.so_what: Colour on the composer's exacting control over performance.
insights.quote: there, to my left, was Steve Reich watching Steve Reich talking on the screen
